issue_context.title: .Net 5 Directory.Delete needs new permissions (vs .Net 4.8)
issue_context.body:
<!--This is just a template - feel free to delete any and all of it and replace as appropriate.-->

### Description
`Directory.Delete(somePath, recursive: true)` throws an `UnauthorizedAccessException` when the user has no `ListDirectory` rights on the parent directory

Repro sample:
```csharp
var parent = Directory.CreateDirectory(@"C:\Temp\someparent");
var ac = parent.GetAccessControl();
ac.SetAccessRule(new FileSystemAccessRule(WindowsIdentity.GetCurrent().User, FileSystemRights.ListDirectory, AccessControlType.Deny));
parent.SetAccessControl(ac);

var subDir = Directory.CreateDirectory(@"C:\Temp\someparent\subdir");
Directory.Delete(subDir.FullName, recursive: true);
```

throws:
```
UnauthorizedAccessException: Access to the path 'C:\Temp\someparent\subdir' is denied.
at System.IO.FileSystem.GetFindData(String fullPath, WIN32_FIND_DATA& findData)
   at System.IO.FileSystem.RemoveDirectory(String fullPath, Boolean recursive)
   at System.IO.Directory.Delete(String path, Boolean recursive)
```
This is unexpected, because:
- the same user created the directory
- the user can still create sub directories and files within the directory
- same code works without exception in .Net 4.8
- the directory can be deleted without the recursive: true option

### Configuration
.NET target: Core 5.0.8, and Framework 48 (4.0.30319.42000)
Operating system: Windows 20H2

### Regression?
Yes the same code example from above works without problems in .Net 4.8

### Other information
In our case, enabling the list permission on the parent directory is not an acceptable solution, due to the security implications.

@Inspyro thank you for a detailed bug report, the problem has been fixed and it's going to be part of .NET 6

review_comments: If this is only compiling on Windows does it really need the `PlatformSpecific` attribute? Perhaps you don't need to make `Directory_Delete_str_bool` partial if you keep the attribute.

I forgot to call `Delete`:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/ec07ac8709dd5676084a79193cac9498eaa427ff/src/libraries/System.IO.FileSystem/tests/Directory/Delete.cs#L229-L232

Which is overriden in subclasses that test `DirectoryInfo` as well:

https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/blob/57bfe474518ab5b7cfe6bf7424a79ce3af9d6657/src/libraries/System.IO.FileSystem/tests/DirectoryInfo/Delete.cs#L27-L37

 fixed that in https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/pull/56996/commits/bd7f5f0ae71213e39803cec44d0a72ee7699c397

Now having this type partial makes sense.

Speaking of using`PlatformSpecific` attribute in files that are conditionally compiled only on certain OSes. I prefer to have the extra attribute, but I don't have a strong opinion about it. @ViktorHofer do we have some guidelines for that?
I agree with @adamsitnik. For such situations we usually move the platform specific code into a separate file.
Do you know why `Path.Join(fullPath, "*")` is needed in `RemoveDirectoryRecursive`?

My understanding is that `FindFirstFile($pathToDirectory)` returns info for given directory, while `FindFirstFile($pathToDirectory/*)` returns info for the first file in given directory (which is needed here as we want to recursively remove all files and subfolders)
Should we also test that the parent directory can be deleted?
We have other tests that verify that. In this particular test I wanted to focus on the lack of `FileSystemRights.ListDirectory`
I don't like this suggestion as it increases code nesting
